decoded:
Saffron Bites catering quote arrived.

Main spread on the 15th has two tiers.

Tier A at $48 per head includes seared tuna canapés, braised short rib station, full dessert display.

Tier B at $37 per head swaps short rib for mushroom Wellington station, cuts dessert display to chocolate torte, berry pavlovas.

My read: stick with Tier A for primary sponsor dinner in the Veridian Room. Could use Tier B for general attendee reception in the Atrium if budget squeezed.

However, the minimum for any single service is 70 guests.

If final headcount in the Veridian Room is under 70, pad with organizing committee members to hit the minimum.

^Only move people to the Atrium list if absolutely necessary. We promised them the full experience.

For the Atrium, if the count is between 70 and 90, Tier B is approved. If the count exceeds 90, switch to Tier A for them as well. The per-head cost difference shrinks with volume, so the upgrade is worth it for a larger crowd.

Timing: they need a final menu selection and guaranteed guest numbers by 5 p.m. this Thursday the 7th. They offered a 3% discount if we wire a 50% deposit by Friday at noon, instead of the following Monday. The remaining balance is due on the 13th.

^Confirm wire details with Aris Finance; use vendor code `CAT-882`. If discount applies, note explicitly on the payment authorization.

^Double-check proposal includes late-night snack delivery for the tech crew at 11 p.m. Separate order: 15 boxed meals (not part of per-head calculation).

Crucially, if we go Tier B anywhere, we must get written confirmation from Saffron Bites that all nut-based ingredients are excluded from the mushroom Wellington filling. The last year incident with the pine nut puree cannot be repeated. Their standard recipe includes it, so this requires a specific amendment.
